## **Extension of the Australian Apprenticeship Support Services**

The Australian Government has extended the Australian Apprenticeship Support Services for a further two-year period from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2028. More information can be found [here.](https://www.apprenticeships.gov.au/who-to-contact/Extension-of-the-Australian-Apprenticeship-Support-Services)

# Changes to Australian Apprenticeships Incentive System from 1 January 2027

From 1 January 2027, support will focus on apprentices and small to medium employers, so help goes where it is needed most.

![](https://content.apprenticeships.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-04/iStock-1189913209.jpg)

## What are the changes?

#### Key Apprenticeship Program Employer Incentive

- The incentive is available from 1 January 2027 for eligible apprenticeships until 30 June 2029 (it is currently due to end on 31 December 2026).
- Payments will change to up to $4,000 (down from $5,000 in 2026). This will be paid in two instalments during the first year of the apprenticeship.
- Employers with 200 or more employees will not be eligible (except Group Training Organisations).

#### Priority Hiring Incentive

- Employers with 200 or more employees will not be eligible (except Group Training Organisations).
- There is no change to the amount of this payment. It will stay at up to $2,500, paid in two instalments during the first year of the apprenticeship.

#### Australian Apprenticeships Priority List

- After feedback from stakeholders in late 2025, we are changing how the Priority List is updated each year so that it:
  - takes both national and regional skills shortages into account, informed by the Occupation Shortage List developed by Jobs and Skills Australia each year
  - considers shortage ratings over two years to improve stability and support business planning
  - matches government priorities and targets support where it is needed most, including construction, net zero, manufacturing, and care and support
  - still includes priority jobs that support women and First Nations communities
- These changes will take place from 1 January 2027. The 2026 Priority List will stay the same for the rest of 2026.

## What’s staying the same?

#### Grandfathering Arrangements

- Eligible employers (including large employers) who start or restart an apprenticeship before 1 January 2027 will keep the current rates: up to $5,000 for the Key Apprenticeship Program Employer Incentive and $2,500 for the Priority Hiring Incentive.

#### Key Apprenticeship Program (KAP) Apprentice Incentive

- Eligible apprentices can receive up to $10,000 (full-time) or $5,000 (part-time) over the course of their apprenticeship when working in the following streams:
  - New Energy Apprenticeship (NEA): Supports Australian Apprentices in the clean energy sector.
  - Housing Construction Apprenticeship (HCA): Supports Australian Apprentices in the housing construction sector.
- paid as follows:
  - Full-time: $2,000 at 6, 12, 24, and 36 months and on completion.
  - Part-time: $1,000 at 6, 12, 24, and 36 months and on completion.

#### Australian Apprentice Training Support Payment (AATSP)

- Apprentices doing a Certificate III or above in a job on the Australian Apprenticeships Priority List, will continue to get up to $2,500 over the first two years of the apprenticeship, until 30 June 2029.

#### Living Away From Home Allowance (LAFHA)

- Australian Apprentices who need to move away from home or become homeless during their apprenticeship.
- Tax-free weekly payments paid at the following rates:
  - 1st year: $125.52 per week
  - 2nd year: $94.14 per week
  - 3rd year: $47.07 per week

#### Australian Apprenticeship Support Loans (AASL)

- Australian Apprentices completing an apprenticeship in an occupation listed on the Priority List.
- What support is available?
  - Interest-free loan up to $27,048 (2026-2027), paid monthly.
  - Repayments start when your income exceeds $69,528 (2026-27 threshold).
  - Loan indexation is capped at the lower of the Wage Price Index or Consumer Price Index.
  - A 20% discount applies on completion of your apprenticeship.

#### Disability Australian Apprentice Wage Support (DAAWS)

- Employers of Australian Apprentices with disability will still be eligible for a weekly support payment of $226.01.

#### DAAWS Off-the-job Tutorial, Mentor, and Interpreter Assistance

- Off-the-job Tutorial, Mentor, and Interpreter Assistance is available to Registered Training Organisations to provide tutorial, mentor and interpreter assistance to apprentices with a disability who are experiencing difficulties with the off-the-job component of their Australian Apprenticeship.
- Tutorial services- $38.50 per hour, up to a maximum of $5,500 per year
- Mentor or interpreter services- $38.50 per hour, up to a maximum of $5,500 per year.

## Need More Information?

Contact an Apprentice Connect Australia Provider. To find a provider in your area visit [Search for an Apprentice Connect Australia Provider](https://www.apprenticeships.gov.au/who-to-contact/search-for-a-provider)
